_comment: Landed rows with an empty stated_schedule after the fetch pass of 7 September 2026.
PRESS_ONLY ENTRIES CARRY THE DATE THEY WERE REFUSED FOR. `press_stated_production_start`
and `press_source_url` are a COMPARISON TIER: sources/export_status_history.py reads them
into two CSV columns and one summary table so the register can be measured against what
the press says, and they are NEVER written into data/transition/projects.json. The point is
to make the cost of the source rule visible rather than to relax it -- the register still
states nothing it cannot source to a company, a permit or a grant decision.
WHY NOT sources/manual/wanted. That queue is for a page a browser can read and the
fetcher is refused, and its README says so. Only stegra-boden is that, and it is filed
there as well as here. The rest are the harder case: the page is readable and no company,
permit or grant decision states a date at all.
`press_only` rows are the ones to watch. A date EXISTS for them and is excluded because
it is trade press. That is the source rules working, not a gap in the research, and the
row's own note already carries the press date as press. If the rule is ever relaxed these
are the rows it would change.
